idea: Neighborhood recycling bin with a camera sorts common contamination items (plastic bags, food waste) out of the recycling stream automatically before pickup, refusing bins more than 10% contaminated and texting the resident why.
source: hand-authored by Claude Sonnet 5, offline in this session, by-layer Slicer variant -- see foundry/tools/slicer.yaml

pieces.text: A camera-based sorter can reliably identify plastic bags and food waste in a mixed recycling stream at the accuracy needed to avoid wrongly refusing clean bins.
The bin can physically or procedurally refuse a load over 10% contaminated -- not close, not get picked up, flag for return -- without a person on-site to intervene.
A text message explaining the specific contamination is enough for most residents to actually change their sorting behavior, rather than being ignored after the first few times.
A camera plus sorting/refusal hardware can be added to a standard recycling bin at a cost the neighborhood or city is willing to pay per bin.
Residents and the city will tolerate the false-refusal rate a camera sorter realistically has, rather than losing trust after a few wrongly-refused clean bins.
